links.outcome: Change in allocation probabilities between paired-context and independent inference after one added patient sentence
links.effect: Across three of four models, paired-context and independent-inference runs showed different probability shifts, often in opposite directions, when new information was provided.
links.quote: Across three of four tested models, the paired-context and independent-inference experiments have different probability shifts, often in opposite directions (in favor of Person B vs. in favor of Person A) when new information is provided.

unlisted_practices: Testing how accumulated conversation context (prior model response retained in context) changes LLM decisions in resource allocation
Context engineering of LLM-based systems used in decision-making

screen.reason: The study empirically tests how different inference setups (paired-context with previous outputs versus independent inference) affect LLM decision stability and bias in medical resource allocation.

primary.practice: context window management / inference setup design
